subtype: College sleep debt and mood swings [Actor]
passage: I'm Vidya, and I share Room 214 in the hostel with Ayesha. This term she has lived on late-night chai and videos in bed, then slept through her morning lectures. Last week she snapped at me for asking about the laundry, then sat on her bed staring at nothing. On Friday she said, "I just feel flat. Maybe I need a new study app, or one of those morning-routine videos." I didn't know what was going on inside her, so I only said, "You've barely slept all week." She looked surprised, as if she hadn't connected the two. Since Sunday she has set one alarm for the same time every day and put the kettle away at night. She's laughing at my jokes again, though I can't say for sure that's why.

qa.q: What did Ayesha snap at Vidya for?
What was Ayesha feeling on Friday, and what did she think would fix it?
qa.a: She felt flat and low, and thought a new study app or morning-routine videos might help, without linking her mood to sleep.

qa.q: Which change seems to have helped, and why?
qa.a: A steady alarm time and putting the kettle away at night; small, regular sleep changes seem to lift her mood more than a motivation trick would.

qa.q: How is Vidya affected by Ayesha's sleepless weeks?
qa.a: Vidya gets snapped at over small things and is unsure what is going on inside Ayesha, but cares enough to point out the missing sleep.

grounding: Shows a hostel student running on late nights and chai, feeling flat and snappy without linking it to sleep, and small sleep changes helping.

subtype: College sleep debt and mood swings [Actor]
passage:
Week one: Jahnavi stayed up with the corridor gang till the small hours, drank cup after cup of cutting chai and skipped the early lab. By evening she was jittery, and she cried over a message from Ojas that only said "ok".
Week three: Ojas found her half asleep in the library. "You're not lazy, you're exhausted. Try one thing: the same wake-up every day, even Sunday." Jahnavi grumbled but set the alarm.
Week six: She still stays up late some nights, but she wakes at the same time and has stopped napping through the afternoon. The "ok" messages don't sting anymore. She told Ojas she feels steadier than any productivity video ever made her.

qa.q: What did Ojas's message say in week one?
Why did Jahnavi cry over the short message?
qa.a: She was exhausted and jittery, so she felt hurt and anxious over something small that would not bother her when rested.

qa.q: What small step did Jahnavi try, and why did it help?
qa.a: Waking at the same time every day, even Sunday; a steady rhythm eased her sleep debt and steadied her mood.

qa.q: How does Ojas see Jahnavi's struggles in week three?
qa.a: Ojas sees exhaustion, not laziness, and offers one simple change instead of a lecture.

grounding: Illustrates a college student's late nights, chai and skipped classes bringing jittery, teary moods, and one regular sleep habit lifting them over weeks.
